problemStatement.formal: For L^2 functions f, g: |integral f*g d mu|^2 <= (integral f^2 d mu) * (integral g^2 d mu)
problemStatement.plain: The integral form of Cauchy-Schwarz (Bunyakovsky-Schwarz inequality): the square of the integral of the product of two square-integrable functions is at most the product of the integrals of their squares.
whyMatters: Fundamental inequality in functional analysis and measure theory
Historical: proved by Bunyakovsky (1859) before Schwarz (1885)
Used in quantum mechanics (uncertainty principle), statistics (correlation bounds)
